attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post, in his own voice, describing the briefing.

semantics.note: The proposition says 'the policy measures' without listing the five needs, but the contract supplies them. Naming Altman and Amodei fits the context. It is a retrospective observation about one day.

contract.note: The plain reading is fair: it allows exceptions and different wording, and treats silence as neutral. The result depends on whether general accountability talk counts as backing legal liability, and on how far 'pretty much everyone' stretches.

evidence.note: UN automatic transcript. Bengio backs pre-deployment safety demonstration, incident reporting, liability insurance, global dialogue and urgency. That supports the claim for one speaker only.
UN automatic transcript. Altman backs international cooperation, standards for assessing risk, and incident reporting. Nothing here on liability. Partial support.

Secondary transcript dated 2026-09-24. Amodei backs external evaluators, testing standards, verification, incident notification and urgent cooperation. Delangue backs transparency. Neither addresses liability. Partial support.

reviews.rationale: The packet shows broad agreement among the briefers on testing, transparency, cooperation and urgency. Only Bengio clearly backs liability, and the other national speakers are mostly not covered. No item shows substantial disagreement, and silence counts for neither side. The official record could not be read, so the spread of agreement across all five needs and nearly all speakers is not settled.
